ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane China>Rider>High Time and relentless NFA jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The set bursts with a scorching China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time segue, then rolls into an extended Not Fade Away/Drums/Good Lovin'/The Other One/Lovelight marathon that never lets up. Jerry’s guitar is on fire and Phil drives the low end with a machine‑gun bass. The audience tape captures the energy despite some hiss and occasional pops.
ai_show_review.review:
March 7, 1970 at the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium captured the Dead in top gear. From the opening “Black Peter” through the blazing “China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time” sequence, Jerry Garcia’s guitar was scorching, his vocals emotive, and Bob Weir’s rhythm work searing. The second half turned into a relentless groove: a first‑time “Not Fade Away” launch into drums, then an unbroken flow of “Good Lovin'”, “The Other One”, and a soaring “Turn On Your Lovelight”. Phil Lesh’s bass was a machine‑gun pulse that kept the momentum driving, while Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann supplied tribal, propulsive drumming. Pigpen’s vocal power added extra grit even though his organ solo was sparse. The sole audience recording (gd70-03-07.aud.hanno.6156.sbeok.shnf) is surprisingly clear for a crowd tape – instrument separation shines through the hiss and occasional splice glitches, making this a must‑listen snapshot of early‑’70 Dead energy.

For fans hunting a vivid snapshot of the band’s high‑octane live chemistry in 1970, this show delivers standout moments without any major musical lulls. While the tape isn’t pristine, its warmth and excitement more than compensate, offering an authentic window into a night where the Dead were truly on fire.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Multiple reviewers praise the performance – scorching guitar, machine‑gun bass, tribal drums and high‑energy segues – with no consistent negative comments about playing. Positive language dominates, yielding a modest +0.7 sentiment boost.

best_recording.reason: Only available recording; good‑quality audience tape with clear instrument separation that captures the high‑energy performance despite minor hiss and splice artifacts.

band_performance.Jerry: Scorching guitar tone with fast‑paced solos and emotive vocals on Black Peter and High Time.
band_performance.Phil: Delivers a machine‑gun bass intro into Good Lovin' and provides a driving low‑end foundation throughout the jams.
band_performance.Bob: Burning rhythm/lead work during the China > Rider sequence, adding to the high‑energy feel of the set.
band_performance.Pigpen: Vocal power is repeatedly highlighted; organ solos are sparse but his presence adds grit to the performance.
band_performance.Mickey: Provides tribal, powerful drumming that propels the Not Fade Away/Drums segment forward.
band_performance.Billy: Matches Mickey with a forceful drum attack, reinforcing the relentless momentum of the second‑half jam.
